objective: Implement a separate minimal session messaging service and CLI so agents can connect to a shared session and exchange messages over a Tailscale-reachable HTTP endpoint.

intent_contract.objective: Create a file-backed HTTP service and CLI that support session connect, send, and read flows using a shared service URL.
success_criteria: A service can create or update a session and persist messages under sessions/<id>.json and messages/<session-id>/*.json.
CLI clients can connect to a session with an agent id, persist that local client session state, and then send and read messages without retyping the session on every command.
End-to-end tests prove a remote client can connect, send, and read through the HTTP service.
non_goals: Do not add project coordination, assignments, inboxes, briefs, derivation logic, or task state machines.
Do not add authentication, Tailscale APIs, or tunnel orchestration in this iteration.
Do not retrofit the Artifact Loop coordination model into this separate package.

ambiguity_classification.statement: The network layer is assumed to be provided externally by Tailscale; the package only needs to be Tailscale-reachable by host and port.

constraints: Keep the implementation isolated to a new session-hub package.
Use plain HTTP + JSON request/response contracts and a --service-url based client flow.
Preserve a minimal operator surface: serve, connect, send, read.

out_of_scope: Any auth, RBAC, inbox, or coordination workflow beyond session messages

implementation_plan: Create a standalone session-hub package with a file-backed store for sessions, messages, and local client state.
Implement a minimal HTTP service with health, connect, send, and read endpoints.
Implement a small CLI that can serve, connect, send, and read while resolving the current local session from client state.
Add integration tests that boot the service and prove end-to-end remote session messaging.

definition_of_done.criterion: Agents can connect to the same session and exchange persisted messages through the shared service using only session id, agent id, and service URL.
Automated tests cover direct service usage and CLI flows with persisted local client state.
The service remains minimal and explicit about having no built-in auth so callers do not assume protected transport or identity verification.
Human-readable CLI output and JSON output let operators confirm the active session, sender, and message history.
The new package is isolated enough that rollback is a bounded deletion/revert of session-hub files only.

failure_mode_matrix.scenario: A client sends without explicit session flags and no local client state exists.
failure_mode_matrix.handling: Fail closed with a clear error telling the operator to connect first or pass --session/--agent.
failure_mode_matrix.verification: CLI integration tests cover connect-first behavior.

failure_mode_matrix.handling: Surface a remote request failure directly and do not write fake local success state.
failure_mode_matrix.verification: Client request helper and integration tests cover remote request failures indirectly through fetch error handling.

edge_case_matrix.scenario: Reading an empty session should not fail.
edge_case_matrix.handling: Return an empty message list and preserve the session metadata.
edge_case_matrix.verification: Service tests validate empty reads after connect.

edge_case_matrix.scenario: Repeated connect by the same agent should refresh last-seen state without duplicating the agent membership.
edge_case_matrix.handling: Upsert the agent entry on connect.
edge_case_matrix.verification: Service tests validate repeated connect behavior.

solution_ladder.description: Patch Artifact Loop messaging primitives to act like generic sessions.
pros: Could reuse existing HTTP client/service code
cons: Would drag in task/project coordination concepts the user explicitly rejected

solution_ladder.description: Extract generic messaging helpers from Artifact Loop into a shared library.
cons: Still spends time untangling the wrong abstraction before proving the simple workflow

solution_ladder.description: Create a separate minimal package with only serve/connect/send/read behavior.
pros: Matches the requested product surface directly
Keeps rollback and future evolution isolated
cons: Duplicates a small amount of HTTP and file-store infrastructure

layer_justification: The user wants a separate, minimal messaging surface with no coordination model. A new isolated package is the highest useful layer that matches that requirement directly.
why_not_lower: Reusing or patching Artifact Loop would keep the wrong task/project semantics attached to the problem.
why_not_higher: A richer multi-agent platform would repeat the overbuilt direction the user explicitly rejected.
future_reuse_gain: If this works, richer agent messaging features can be added on top of a clean session/message operating surface rather than stripped out of a coordination engine.
